title: Billing & Metering Audit Playbook — SOC-ready retention, RBAC, and rate-limit proofs
creator: Asha Patel
description: Objective: Produce a repeatable, auditable playbook and evidence bundle proving correctness of billing/metering, rate limiting, quotas, and usage accounting for SOC-type audits and financial reviews. Scope includes event capture, aggregation logic, rate-limit/quota enforcement logs, retention/immutable storage, access controls, and reconciliation procedures. Deliverables: 1) Playbook document (confluence) mapping controls to SOC criteria and internal policies; 2) Immutable audit log bucket with lifecycle and retention policy; 3) Automated reconciliation job with alerting and test harness; 4) Evidence bundle for audits (sample invoices, reconciliation reports, access logs, PRs, runbooks). Exclusions: upstream cloud billing provider invoices are out of scope (we reconcile at token/usage level).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Confluence playbook created and linked in attachments. 2) Immutable audit logs for metering events enabled (S3 Object Lock + KMS) with documented retention policy in playbook. 3) End-to-end reconciliation job runs daily and reports drift metrics; historical report for the last 90 days available. 4) RBAC and MFA enforced for any access to audit artifacts; access review runbook documented. 5) Test harness reproduces a synthetic billing session and shows accounting delta < 0.01% vs canonical aggregator. 6) Mapping table of artifacts to SOC control IDs included in evidence bundle.
task_list: Draft playbook outline and SOC mapping
Define exact retention periods for: raw event stream, aggregated usage, invoices, and rate-limit logs
Configure immutable audit bucket and set object lock + KMS policy
Implement access-journal service to record admin actions on billing resources
Build reconciliation pipeline (event -> aggregated units -> billing units) and smoke tests
Create automated daily report and PagerDuty alert for drift > 0.1%
Prepare evidence bundle with PRs, runbooks, dashboards, and sample reconciliations
Peer review of playbook and technical design with Security/Compliance

verification_plan: 1) Run nightly reconciliation job against production sample window and compare with canonical ledger; check drift threshold. 2) Execute tamper-test: create, attempt modify, and detect modification of audit object in staging (should be blocked or recorded). 3) Run access review playbook and verify that only approved principals have READ/WRITE. 4) Provide evidence artifact package and run internal audit checklist (Confluence checklist).
risks: 1) KMS key policy complexity could delay object-lock enforcement. 2) High-volume raw event retention increases storage costs — need cost approval for 7-year retention. 3) Edge-case rounding differences between streaming aggregator and batch calculator can cause audit deltas. 4) Rate-limit logs may be trimmed at ingress if retention misconfigured; must ensure separate log sink.
mitigations: 1) Engage SecOps early to standardize KMS policy and HSM-backed key if required. 2) Propose tiered retention: full fidelity 2 years, aggregated metrics 7 years; present costs to Finance. 3) Implement deterministic aggregation algorithm and unit tests; add tolerance to reconciliation alerts. 4) Add dedicated logging pipeline (Kafka -> archive sink) for rate-limit and quota events with guaranteed retention policy.
notes: Playbook should also include guidance for Dedicated and Private customers (on-prem) describing how to provide equivalent evidence (local audit exports, signed manifests). Coordinate with Solutions Engineering for customer-facing templates.
